# Pattern Matching with case Statements

The `case` statement provides high-performance pattern matching without invoking subshells:

```bash
case "$os_type" in
    ubuntu|debian)
        pkg_mgr="apt-get"
        ;;
    fedora|rhel|centos)
        pkg_mgr="dnf"
        ;;
    alpine)
        pkg_mgr="apk"
        ;;
    arch)
        pkg_mgr="pacman"
        ;;
    *)
        echo "Unsupported distribution: $os_type" >&2
        exit 1
        ;;
esac
```

### Advanced Terminators in Bash

* `;;`: Terminates execution (standard).
* `;&`: Fall-through to the next clause without testing its pattern.
* `;;&`: Tests subsequent patterns and executes if matched.
